rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the eight-compound elution window and identify critical pairs while limiting the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The results will guide a narrower, faster gradient and temperature optimization.

Test temperature selectivity while holding the gradient fixed, targeting the crowded middle cluster and final pair. The current short elution window leaves room to use a shallower gradient after identifying a favorable temperature.

Probe the low-temperature end with the same gradient to assess whether selectivity improves for the middle cluster and late peaks. This completes a broad temperature screen before refining gradient slope.
Use a shallower gradient at the best temperature to test whether the two remaining critical pairs separate. The current last peak at 7.23 minutes provides some room to trade speed for resolution.
Shorten the fully resolving gradient by one grid step to bring the last peak below 10 minutes. This tests whether the critical pair retains R ≥ 1.5 and achieves the maximum CRF.

Raise the starting and ending organic fractions together, preserving the slope of the fully resolving method while moving elution earlier. This targets a last peak below 10 minutes without the slope increase that compromised the critical pair.
Slightly reduce the gradient slope to lift the critical pair above R = 1.5. The 0.75-minute margin before the time penalty should accommodate the modest retention increase.

The maximum CRF is already secured by injection 7; now test a shorter elution window. Raising the starting organic fraction should advance elution, while a slightly shallower slope should help preserve critical-pair resolution.

Test a one-step temperature increase to shorten the fully resolved method from injection 8. Monitor both the marginal middle pair and the temperature-sensitive late pair, retaining injection 8 as the faster maximum-score fallback.

Return to 25 °C and raise the starting organic fraction to advance elution. Use a shallower slope to counter the loss of middle-pair resolution seen when increasing the starting fraction, aiming for full resolution before 8.90 minutes.

Test whether a 5 °C increase resolves the marginal middle pair while shortening elution. The larger preceding gap in injection 10 may accommodate the temperature-driven convergence that limited injection 9.

Lengthen the gradient by one step to improve the sole unresolved pair in injection 11 while keeping elution comfortably below 10 minutes. Check that the neighboring middle pair and final pair retain their full-resolution margins.

The maximum score is already secured, so screen an intermediate high temperature for a potentially faster selectivity window. The 40 and 60 °C runs showed substantial shifts in the crowded groups, leaving 50 °C worth testing before further refinement.

Test a shallower gradient at 50 °C to shift selectivity within the unresolved middle cluster. The last peak at 5.87 minutes leaves substantial room to improve resolution while keeping elution below 10 minutes.

Combine the shallower gradient with 60 °C to test whether temperature separates the persistent middle co-elution and moves the late pair away from its crossing. This may provide a faster fully resolved alternative while the maximum-score methods remain available.

Shorten the 60 °C gradient by one step to move the unresolved late-middle pair away from its apparent convergence at longer gradients. The early cluster should retain much of the resolution gained at 20 minutes, potentially giving full resolution with faster elution.

Use a slope of 0.045 organic fraction per minute, just steeper than injection 16, to lift the R = 1.49 pair while preserving the two marginal early separations. The gradient should extend beyond the last peak, so the lower endpoint provides fine slope control without affecting elution.

Raise the starting organic fraction to shorten elution, using a shallower gradient to compensate for potential loss of early-cluster resolution. Injection 17 remains the fastest demonstrated maximum-score method.

Make the gradient one step shallower to recover the early critical pair at the higher starting organic fraction. Monitor the late-middle pair closely, since previous slope reductions improved the early cluster but narrowed that separation.

Test whether a lower starting organic fraction permits a steeper gradient while preserving early-cluster resolution. This explores a potentially faster alternative to injection 17, with particular attention to its marginal early pairs.

Increase the slope slightly from 0.045 to 0.04583 per minute to test the speed boundary around injection 17. This should improve the late-middle separation but may bring an early pair just below R = 1.5.

Seek a maximum-score method with more resolution margin by slightly lengthening injection 10’s gradient at 25 °C. Its late pairs had ample separation, so this should improve the sole critical pair without the late-pair convergence observed at 30 °C.

Add one gradient-duration step to injection 8 to increase its narrow resolution margin while targeting a last peak below 10 minutes. This tests a more tolerant maximum-score alternative; injection 17 remains the fastest fully resolved method demonstrated.

Extend injection 22 by one step to increase its critical-pair resolution while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. This refines a maximum-score alternative with greater separation margin, while injection 17 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method.

Use the final injection to test a slightly shallower gradient predicted to raise the minimum resolution above 2 while keeping the last peak under 10 minutes. The maximum CRF is already secured, and injection 17 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method.
